answers.text: We have been nomadic as people in the past, and people in other countries are already experiencing this.
answers.author: You

answers.text: This scenario was very jarring, it is already happening to many communities.
answers.author: You

answers.text: The mental health component of moving is missing.
answers.author: You

questions.label: What feels most important or distinctive?

answers.text: People owned their own data, as a piece of property.  That is very different from where we are today.
answers.author: You

answers.text: The scenarios of what you can do with the data are distinctive.  What would motivate someone to keep their data private, vs sell it?  How does that impact the data institutions have?
answers.author: You

questions.label: What feels unclear, incomplete, or difficult to understand?

answers.text: Despite having an AI navigator, uncertainty about location still makes things difficult.
answers.author: You

answers.text: What is the role of paper documents?  Feels incongruent with the rest of the scenario.
answers.author: You

answers.text: Doesn't include the emotional and financial component of moving.
answers.author: You

answers.text: How do jobs work?
answers.author: You

answers.text: Who stays behind, who leaves?
answers.author: You

questions.label: What assumptions does the scenario appear to make?

answers.text: That it is easy to move.
answers.author: You

answers.text: Funding and services shift based on where displaced people register.  This is different from how things currently work.
answers.author: You

answers.text: Assumption that state borders are not a barrier, and there is a seamless ability to access service across state lines.
answers.author: You

answers.text: There seems to be universal care of some sort, insurance doesn't matter, out of network doesn't matter.
answers.author: You

questions.label: Is anything important missing that would need to be true for this future to make sense?

answers.text: A lot of change in the space of health records, potentially universal healthcare.
answers.author: You

questions.label: Stepping into the future — It is now several years into this future. What has become normal that would feel unusual today?

answers.text: Location based community is no longer at the center of how we organize ourselves.  As communities are impacted differently, some may become closer and some may become weaker.
answers.author: You

answers.text: Having AI provide navigation services is normal.
answers.author: You

answers.text: State assistance may become more normalized and accepted.  On the contrary, rich communities insulated from disaster may become even more separate.
answers.author: You

answers.text: Any major population level data collection, like the census, the ACS.  Surveys based on geography.
answers.author: You

answers.text: Home insurance is not working, it can be discontinued.  This is true today.
answers.author: You

answers.text: Jurisdictional lines.
answers.author: You

answers.text: Ownership and access to your own health data.
answers.author: You

answers.text: Long term planning is much more challenging if funding follows people who move frequently.
answers.author: You

questions.label: What do people now expect from institutions?

answers.text: Expect more from public health systems.  Possibly more than public health is capable of.  They may become frustrated that public health cannot keep up.
answers.author: You

answers.text: Expect to receive services when they move.
answers.author: You

questions.label: What additional thoughts should be captured that are different about this future?

answers.text: Today with disasters, you typically deal with a human, but in this scenario there is an AI navigator who has influence and authority.
answers.author: You

answers.text: Does public health play a coordination role across various agencies?  Or does another body do that, like the military?
answers.author: You

answers.text: What does trust building look like when communities are always changing?
answers.author: You

answers.text: AI may have absorbed some of what CHWs currently do.  Something is lost here if that happens.
answers.author: You

answers.text: The benevolence is missing from AI, how can public health fill this gap?
answers.author: You

answers.text: Individuals control access to their health data. Providers and public health don't automatically have access.
answers.author: You

answers.text: Funding follows people and shift as displaced people register in new places
answers.author: You

answers.text: Losing the human/relational component
answers.author: You

answers.text: Disparities in public health capacity might be a bigger issue if population size/need shift commonly
answers.author: You

answers.text: Certain services, like access to medications, become easier to access across sytems/jurisdictions
answers.author: You

answers.text: Continuity of care is established/resources move with displaced people instead of forcing people to start over in each place
answers.author: You

answers.text: Public safety might be challenged for those who remain behind
answers.author: You

answers.text: The lack of population level data makes it hard to measure and monitor. Skewed data.
answers.author: You

answers.text: Funding follows people, but how does that affect the places they left. The PH workforce will have to be transient too.
answers.author: You

answers.text: AI is an integral part of people's experience of the health care system
answers.author: You

answers.text: Disease monitoring / tracking is incomplete when people own their health data
answers.author: You

answers.text: Crowding could create environments for disease. and other transient population impacts.
answers.author: You

answers.text: How are people getting public health information - through AI
answers.author: You

answers.text: How do we elect our government officials
answers.author: You

answers.text: State and local borders are weakened, have less impact over peoples lives
answers.author: You

answers.text: What does census data look like in this scenario. (collected more frequently? completely irrelevant?)
answers.author: You

answers.text: Public health services have to rapidly scale up and scale back based on migration into/out of communities
answers.author: You

answers.text: Personal ownership of data means that population level monitoring is difficult, for instance limiting disease tracking.
answers.author: You

answers.text: Transient population leading to: Funding issues, long term planning and building stable infrastructure, census data/tracking, etc.
answers.author: You

answers.text: Continuity of care and access to services, like medication, is improved, which could improve health.
answers.author: You

answers.text: Disparities grow. This impacts the safety of communities people leave, disease outbreaks in crowed areas, and disparities between parts of the country experiencing lots of disasters and stable areas.
answers.author: You

answers.text: In this future, AI plays a key role in navigation and access to information. Which can improve efficiency but lower the sense that someone cares about you.
answers.author: You

answers.text: Community is less defined as the population is more transient, which can affect social cohesion and social capital.
answers.author: You

cards.text: Personal ownership of data means that population level monitoring is difficult, for instance limiting disease tracking.
Transient population leading to: Funding issues, long term planning and building stable infrastructure, census data/tracking, etc.
Continuity of care and access to services, like medication, is improved, which could improve health.
Disparities grow. This impacts the safety of communities people leave, disease outbreaks in crowed areas, and disparities between parts of the country experiencing lots of disasters and stable areas.
In this future, AI plays a key role in navigation and access to information. Which can improve efficiency but lower the sense that someone cares about you.
Community is less defined as the population is more transient, which can affect social cohesion and social capital.

Continuity of care is more than just access to medicine.  Access to prescriptions may be easier, but moving would disrupt the continuity of care resulting from having a trusted relation for a medical provider
Statement 4 about disparities includes a bunch of different topics.  Would like to focus in on the disaster implications.
Online communities can still be strong.  Community may still exist but become less geographically oriented
Community is already changing.  A lot of community is online.  This is already happening without people moving geographically.  For instance - antivax community is mostly online and has a huge impact
Resources are not where they need to be.
Historically underserved communities continue to be underserved or it worsens.
Public health has an incomplete picture for understanding population health outcomes / trends
There is a financial incentive to selling your health data rather than keeping it private
What public health understands about the public will be biased toward those who sell their data
Public health programs, interventions, and services will better meet the needs of those who sell their data
People are more isolated, have fewer people they trust, and lack a sense of belonging
Those with more agency, voice and money have (even more) control over where resources are placed
Spending on disaster response and recovery may increase without improvement to health and safety outcomes
More climate-stable areas will see an influx of displaced communities
Rates of mental illness and substance use increase
More climate-stable areas may see growth in housing, jobs, incomes. These areas might not be on the coasts and may see new relevance/power.
even greater economic and public health disparities between the haves and have-nots
Online/virtual communities become more powerful in shaping health beliefs and behaviors
more and more extreme views to circulate and become nomalized
Climate-stable areas see increased demand on housing
Climate-stable areas see increased demand on health systems
Public health's role as advocate and community organizer becomes more important.
a less effective public health response, which then undermines trust in public health responses
Increased investment in infrastructure within climate stable areas
Lower-income residents of climate stable areas might be pushed out as demand grows.  May be pushed to climate instable areas
It becomes more difficult to come to political consensus leading to an inability to solve societal problems.
Greater difficulty accessing timely care
Greater demand for health providers in climate stable areas
those with more power, money and influence to have even greater power, money and influence
This enhances political capital of communities that can now organize better than they could geographically.
data not being representative, as those with fewer resources will more likely be the ones selling their data, while those with more resources can afford it keep it private
Harmful narratives about groups that have been marginalized are challenged and break down
Leads to innovation in service delivery and ultimately better ways to advance health.
Decline in systemic discrimination
Fewer major cities with more people living in them
Public Health will likely have to become better community organizers, and organize in new ways as communities change
People may delay care because they feel less comfortable seeking out the care they need.
If people don't feel like they belong in their communities they are less likely to participate in the political process.
As views become more extreme more voices for the center become prominent too.
Policies / leadership not representative of displaced communities
Revolution and replacement with a more fair and democratic system.
New leaders that focus on solving societal problems are elected en masse
Less disparities and improved health outcomes.
Less focus on prevention more focus on cure.
Greater emphasis on qualitative methods to understand community needs.
available data does not reflect reality, contributes to misdirection of resources
Builds trust with communities as PH become more embedded and engaging.
data sold is accessed by more than just public health.  people are targeted and advertised to based on their health data.
Individuals balance financial incentives with privacy concerns when sharing / selling their data
Increased need for/demand on environmental health programs
Increased interest in preventive/ public health strategies to reduce demand
Expansion in telehealth services
Overcrowding, disease burden, crime increase
as smaller cities in climate stable areas  grow, we learn from past mistakes and build healthier cities, with cleaner infrastructure
Workforce development/ pipeline strategies that are differently focused
Broader investment in public health infrastructure
more money to be spent on mental health and substance use disorder
Decrease in chronic disease
an influx of new professionals and new ideas that lead to care breakthroughs
better integration between physical and mental health care providers, as well as social services
More emergency care utilization
Public health becomes more effective at communicating with virtual communities
Increased trust and confidence in public health among adversely impacted communities
Public health targeted by those with power
